 This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1.

The claimants, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. It is the case of the claimant that the deceased suffered an accident and he was hospitalized for 7 (seven) days and thereafter he passed away.
It is not in dispute that the deceased passed away on 19.03.2015 and the claim petition initiated by him was continued by his legal representatives.

It is,
therefore, contended that the death has occurred due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The Tribunal has committed serious error in holding that the nexus had not been proved.
3. It is nodoubt true that the claimant was discharged from Victoria Hospital from 13.03.2015.
However, the case records would not indicate that he had some serious injuries which probably resulted in his death.
There is no evidence indicating that the death was a direct consequence of the injuries suffered by him.
4. The Tribunal, was therefore, justified in coming to the conclusion that the nexus of the claimant's death with the accident has not been established.

It is to be noticed here that though no compensation could be awarded for the death of the claimant, but nevertheless, the claimant is Sri. Dasthagir @ Syed Dasthagir Valli vs The Divisional Manager on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134161396/
2 entitled for the injuries that he suffered as a result of the accident.

sentences.text: 5. The Discharge Summary of Sanjay Gandhi Institute, where the claimant was admitted initially on 03.01.2015 and discharged on 08.12.2015 indicates that the claimant had suffered a fracture of left medial malleolus, fibula shaft, head fracture, abrasion injuries over left leg and other injuries over the body.
It is, thus, clear that the medical evidence indicates three major fractures to the claimant.

In this view of the matter, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'.
6.
The evidence on record would also indicate that the claimant was hospitalized on three occasions from January 2015 totally amounting to almost 40 days.

Since the claimant was hospitalised for more than a month, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'conveyance,
attendant charges, food and nourishment'.
7. The amount of Rs.20,000/- awarded by Tribunal under the head 'medical expenses' is just and proper and is affirmed.

8. As the claimant was laid up for almost two months, it would be appropriate to determine the laid up period as three months and award a sum of Rs.27,000/- (Rs.9,000/- x 3 ) towards 'loss of income during laid up period.

9. Thus, the legal representatives of the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 75,000/-
 Conveyance, attendant charges,
 2. 50,000/-
 food and nourishment  3. Loss of income during laid up 27,000/-
 period  4.

Medical expenses 20,000/-
 Total 1,72,000/-
10.

Thus, the appellants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.1,72,000/- as against Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
